heading: Battle
notes: Only deployed military enter maximum raid calculation; worker count is not multiplied. Battle grants one chosen resource benefit.

heading: Coffffee House
notes: Multiplayer passed-last production is implemented. The solo clause is outside the implemented multiplayer model; no shadow opponent machinery was found.

heading: Grand Duchy of Finland
notes: Grand Duchy of Finland is absent from the available card class roster; this promo cannot be played in this snapshot.

heading: Bonus
notes: Bonus sums all completed-card bonuses, increases the chosen standard resource, and reduces VP resource payment with a zero floor; cannot gain resources from over-discounting.

heading: Antikythera Mechanism
notes: Antikythera Mechanism is absent; draw-until-building/wonder, mandatory placement and natural-wonder stopping clauses cannot arise.

heading: Arabian Nights
notes: Passed-over hook grants exactly two books, special branch ignores Golden Age bonus and end-round removes its extra card and hooks. Solo clause outside supported mode.

heading: Le Vite
notes: Special option directly adds three public architects and its discount hook; Golden Age bonus never enters this branch.

heading: Uncle Tom's Cabin
notes: All players including purchaser lose building cards with printed deployment_cost -1. Removal undeploys workers and leaves a vacant replaceable slot, the digital equivalent of a flipped card. Special option ignores Golden Age bonus.

heading: Assassin
notes: Requires a deployed Assassin worker; after-bought-card effect follows ordinary battle gain; each other player chooses legal food payment or advisor removal. Zhu Xi special remove-with behavior discards him whether or not he carries a replacement.

heading: Wonder
notes: Placement permits any replaceable completed wonder slot even when a slot is empty. wonder-ready hooks execute before old wonder removal, so its ready-trigger reward still occurs on replacing it. Mechanical Turk exception outside scope: card absent.

heading: Colosseum
notes: Ready effect invokes mandatory resource loss, not affordability gating; missing food incurs books and resource-deficit VP through ordinary lose_resources.

heading: Great Lighthouse
notes: Actual card-price event tests gold==3, independent of printed row; Hannibal surcharge contributes to card price so row-two battles qualify. Separate Axumite transfer is not part of card price.

heading: Sphinx
notes: Sphinx registers only on ready, so does not award itself five stone; later wonder-ready hooks fire before replacement removes it.

heading: Solomon's Temple
notes: Awards once at each end-of-age and removes on defeat, yielding at most four VP. Strict timing wording says same time as Books, but hook actually executes after end-of-round hooks following Books. No demonstrated outcome difference for this entry; record timing qualification.

heading: Terracotta Army
notes: Placed effect snapshots least stability and applies mandatory four-gold loss to every qualifying player including owner.

heading: Petra
notes: Once-per-round affordable special action pays one food and directly grants chosen three books/gold/stone from supply; no other player involved.

heading: Great Library
notes: Golden Age bonus uses common summed mechanism. Least-stability hook registered on placement removes card on ordinary least checks, including ties.

heading: Alhambra
notes: One private architect is replenished per round and available through ordinary hire actions and costs, rather than a repeatable special action.

heading: Notre Dame
notes: Cross-reference Most and least: produce checks owner.most_stability and grants extra books only for qualifying most set; ties follow shared common most/least algorithm.

heading: Porcelain Tower
notes: Tower cover hooks allow advisor on Tower and replacement of that covering advisor. Global advisor loss collects both completed advisors. Removing just covering advisor reveals Tower; placing ready wonder removes Tower and its covered advisor stack. Self-removing Qin or Hypatia calls remove(self), retaining the other advisor: no Tower remove-with hook propagates this. Whether official any-effect wording includes self-removal needs clarification; ordinary lose-advisor effects remove both as required.

heading: Angkor Wat
notes: Cross-reference Most and least: production tests owner.least_military; tied least share penalty under common algorithm.

heading: Chichen Itza
notes: Buying-war hook immediately adds one VP with no military, war outcome or defeated-player requirement.

heading: Great Wall
notes: Spared-war-point hook protects only direct defeat VP. War resources and their separate deficit VP remain ordinary losses.

heading: Piazza San Marco
notes: Pays two gold to supply and grants chosen five books/food/stone; requires affordability and one action per round.

heading: Hagia Sophia
notes: Hagia Sophia absent from playable card roster; cross-referenced most/least behavior cannot be evaluated for this promo.

heading: Shwedagon Pagoda
notes: Markers and added stability clear at end of round before final scoring. Additionally clears immediately when removed, ending round-long benefit early; previously documented author replacement exception.

heading: Sistine Chapel
notes: Books are attached to hire-architect event. Normal hire actions require an incomplete wonder, so player cannot hire solely to generate books. Free architect completion path also emits the hook; FAQ entry does not explicitly settle free-hire distinction.

heading: Versailles
notes: Force-least effect alters comparison rather than resource marker, preserving actual stability for war mitigation. Effect clears at round end, but removal unregisters it early: previously documented replacement exception.

heading: Potala Palace
notes: bonus_points called by final score and counts owned completed advisors including advisor covering Porcelain Tower; two advisors yield two bonus VP.

heading: Royal Society
notes: Free deployment bypasses only stone payment, calls normal military.deploy and production, retaining immediate and production upkeep.

heading: Uraniborg
notes: Golden Age/Bonus cross-reference: printed bonus2 is summed through common routine, applying only ordinary resource benefit or zero-floored VP price.

heading: Himeji Castle
notes: Replaced-card hook requires both old and new building types and strictly newer new_card.age, then grants four stone at placement. Does not reward same age, military, or empty slot.

heading: Red Fort
notes: buy-card-for-gold event compares actual price==1, not row; grants two food immediately.

heading: Kremlin
notes: Kremlin absent from implemented card roster; ongoing strongest bonus clause cannot arise.

heading: Mechanical Turk
notes: Mechanical Turk absent. VP ownership, transfer placement choice, nonreplacement and reserved natural-wonder-space restrictions cannot arise in this source.

heading: Öresund Dues
notes: Passed-over hook grants two stone per skipped turn. Solo zero-gain clause outside supported multiplayer model.

heading: South Pole Expedition
notes: Mandatory five-food loss on ready uses ordinary deficit payment, allowing completion without five food and charging books/VP as appropriate.

heading: Big Ben
notes: Final bonus counts only self.owner.colony_cards filtered age4; does not count other nations colonies.

heading: Brandenburg Gate
notes: Ready effect grants both six gold and six stone to entire eligible most-military set, including builder.

heading: British Museum
notes: Placed effect imposes ten-book loss on all qualifying least military including owner.

heading: MIT
notes: Bought-building hook follows placement and optionally deploys one worker on that exact card for no stone. If none undeployed it first asks for undeployment; normal deployment effects then apply.

heading: Statue of Liberty
notes: Final scoring correctly delays bonus. Five-player generic most_least can award two players, or tied first when exactly two, rather than strict singleton most workers. Individual wording says more than all others, but general official five-player rule says two most of anything, so priority needs rules clarification; observed code behavior is certain, discrepancy interpretation uncertain.

heading: Titanic
notes: Iterates reverse player order. Removes both advisors on removal option; no advisors forces mandatory four-gold loss with ordinary deficit books/VP. An unaffordable gold option is not offered when advisors provide a payable alternative.

heading: Natural Wonders
notes: Natural-wonder and extension spaces are excluded from replacement; purchase gates sufficient replaceable space, completion actions require replaceable space, and ordinary wonders remain replaceable by natural wonders.

heading: Vesuvius
notes: End-of-age hook returns one worker; existing undeployed worker used if available, otherwise asks to undeploy. Undeploy check suppressed until restored population-track stability. Extra check within end-age hook is not a conflict with this specific mandatory-return entry.

heading: Siberia
notes: Extra-space hook reserves two replaceable spaces at purchase. Discovery places ordinary Siberia then creates and places its extension in another replaceable slot; both are nonreplaceable natural-wonder types.

heading: Sahara
notes: Four extra military emitted exclusively to war-defeat calculation; resources military and ordinary most/least/order/colony checks unchanged.

heading: Hawaii
notes: On placed Hawaii records selected population pool, takes worker without immediate upkeep then marks pool; permanent marker subtracts resource cost and prevents returning that waived slot. Worker identity abstracted by pool bookkeeping.

heading: Spice Islands
notes: Extra-growth-resource hook returns four only in resource-choice branch, applied to selected same resource. Worker-growth branch does not use it.

heading: Titusville
notes: Extra scoring stone inserted only immediately around resource-total division, after card bonus VP; no doubling of ordinary production, military or stability.

heading: Victoria Falls
notes: Row-four colonies created on discovery and never carried into next progress board; progress phase reconstructs three rows. FAQ says discard at end of round whereas source retains board until next progress phase. No established intervening gameplay effect, but literal timing differs.

heading: Uluru
notes: Entry solely specifies solo zero reward. Uluru counts passed players normally, but shadow solo game is not implemented; solo-specific clause cannot arise in supported mode.

heading: Event
notes: Common most/least supports positive exclusion on ties and all negative least; five-player maximum two positive vs all negative cutoff ties. Mandatory choices generally reverse order. Event loss uses raw lose_resources without war stability mitigation. Per-effect single execution and explicit multi-worker loops. Return-worker effects distinct from undeploy effects.

heading: Ashokas conversion
notes: Reverse-order loop permits repeated military undeployment until Done; workers move to undeployed supply rather than population, and are available next round.

heading: Bronze Age Collapse
notes: Safe set is union of most military and most stability, so strongest, most stable and player who is both avoid VP loss.

heading: Christianity
notes: Shared may_pay_to_gain asks Yes/No once per affordable player in reverse order; no mandatory conversion.

heading: Han dynasty
notes: Yes/No wraps both worker and three food; requires worker availability, grants both or neither.

heading: Hellenism
notes: If strongest shared in 2-4, most set empty and others loop makes everyone lose two food; ordinary five-player cutoff rule inherited.

heading: Jain Ascetism
notes: Lost-to-war event accumulates direct and deficit VP per player. Most stable regains only own accumulated lost VP, never others. Resource-loss routine pays available resources before deficits.

heading: Olympic games
notes: Events occur after normal player-order phase. In five-player two most stable are sorted by stability then existing player order and prepended strongest first.

heading: Qin Unifcation
notes: No war means no effect. Otherwise every player with raw military strictly greater than war_value gains one VP.

heading: Spartacus revolt
notes: Event reordering resolves after normal military/stability player-order phase.

heading: Rigveda
notes: Counters record purchases of wars/battles and award one book each at event resolution. FAQ immediate-book suggestion is optional physical tracking convenience, not a required immediate payout.

heading: Sea Peoples
notes: Removal offered only when first wonder under construction has positive completed_stages, then decrements that. Private available architect count is never touched.

heading: Zoroastrian revival
notes: Choice offered to unique most stable (none on shared-most in 2-4). Five-player most stable set sorted by value/current order, top makes shared reward-versus-others-loss choice.

heading: Black Death
notes: Normal case returns worker to chosen population pool and restores upkeep. When no population worker has been taken, source uses extra_worker_pool for the worker placed atop a full track; take_worker consumes that free extra worker first, preserving game-state effect. Track-choice identity is unnecessary digital bookkeeping.

heading: Ecological Collapse
notes: All decisions gathered in reverse order before order mutation; food<2 forces nonpayment. Result keeps paying subgroup in order followed by nonpaying subgroup in order. Event resolves after normal order.

heading: Feudal dues
notes: On reveal skip-player-order hook causes normal order phase to return unchanged; event A intentionally no-op.

heading: Fourth Crusade
notes: Top most-military chooser sorted by value and current order gates all least-military losses. Only when top pays can second most optionally pay for own VP. Generic least set supplies both weakest in five-player and cutoff ties. Affordability and declining properly suppress losses.

heading: Hajj from Mali
notes: At two or fewer gold does nothing; only gold>2 is reduced to exactly two.

heading: Iconoclasm
notes: Single Resources loss includes food -2 and gold -2 simultaneously; both components paid, with normal deficit handling.

heading: Peace of God
notes: Explicit no-war guard exits without granting books.

heading: Song Resistance
notes: Lost-to-war counters record own actual resource and point changes including shortfall penalties, then restore both to most-stable eligible owner.

heading: Stupor Mundi
notes: Counts all bought Golden Ages this round and chooses most at resolution. Keeping physical cards beside board is represented by counter; no physical retention necessary.

heading: Zanj Revolt
notes: Reorders during event after normal player-order phase.

heading: Absolute Monarchy
notes: No standalone discard-advisor main action exists; replacing advisor is via buying and placing new advisor. Event itself penalizes antiquity/medieval advisor without offering discard escape.

heading: Dutch Revolt
notes: Event moves least stable to back after normal player-order phase.

heading: Glorious revolution
notes: Optional Yes/No wraps six gold plus going last. Five-player sorted top-two queried in reverse (secondmost first); accepted players inserted in most/secondmost order at tail, leaving secondmost last when both accept.

heading: Janissaries
notes: Affordability requires two available workers; one Yes/No wraps two take-worker calls plus four stone, so cannot take partial bundle.
